(By Sri. V. Srihari Naidu - Adv.)
 Judgment

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 15.03.2021 at about 9.00 am., when the (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.2477/2021 petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA- 42-H-3014 along with his school going children as pillion riders slowly, carefully and cautiously by observing all traffic rules and regulations on the extreme left side of Ramanahalli - Mudavadi road and when he reached near Shaneshwaraswamy temple, Ramanahalli, Ramanagara taluk and district, at that time, rider of another Hero Splendor + motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA-42-EB-9619 ridden the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner without following any traffic rules and regulations so as to endanger human, all of a sudden came to its wrong side of the road from opposite direction and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to said impact, the petitioner was thrown out from the motor cycle and sustained severe injuries and his motor cycle also damaged.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Dr.Chandramma Dayanand Sagar Hospital, Harohalli wherein he took treatment as inpatient and also (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.2477/2021 underwent surgery.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing agriculture and milk vending and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

The said accident occurred due to sole negligence of the rider of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-42-EB-9619 and the Bidadi police have registered a case against the rider of the said motor cycle in their crime No.0083/2021 under Section 279, 337 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 being the RC owner and the respondent No.2 being its insurer are jointly and severally are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

3. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 and the respondent No.2 has appeared through their counsel and respondent No.2 has filed its objections to the main petition.
4.
The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law or on facts of the same.
It has (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.2477/2021 admitted the issuance of the policy in respect of Motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-42-EB-9618.
Respondent No.2 has denied the involvement of the Motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-42-EB-9618 in the alleged accident.

Further contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper parties and the rider and along with 2 pillion riders were not wearing helmet and without driving licence Ramesh Alias Ramesh V vs Nagesh Y on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175650736/
2 ride the same on the date of accident.

Further deposed that, the owner of the vehicle did not report and furnished the RTO documents pertaining to the motor cycle regarding the driving licence of the person who was driving the vehicle at the time of accident which required under Section 134(C) and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.158(6) of MV Act.
It has contented that, at the time of accident, the driver of the motor cycle does not posses valid and effective driving licence to drive the (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.2477/2021 same.
Further contended that, the accident occurred due to the contributory negligence of rider of both motor cycles.

Further contended that,
compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant and fanciful.
With these grounds the respondent No.2 sought for rejecting the claim petition.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 15.03.2021 at about 9.00 am., near Shaneswaraswamy temple,
Ramanahalli-Mudavadi raod, Ramanahalli village, Ramanagara, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent act of riding of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-42-EB-9619 by its rider as alleged in the petition ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1, one MRO has examined as PW.2 and Dr. S.A.Somashekara has examined as PW.3 and in all got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P.18.
On the other hand, the Deputy Manager - Legal has examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 3 and closed their side evidence.
7. Heard arguments and perused the materials available on record.

11.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1.
In his cross-examination he has specifically denied the suggestions made by the learned counsel for the respondent regarding, by his own negligence the alleged accident occurred.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has not elicited anything (SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.2477/2021 from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of rider of the offending motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-42-EB-9619 which belongs to the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is its insurer.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.2477/2021 several facts like injuries, pain and suffering, sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.

b) Towards Medical Expenses: Petitioner has produced 38 medical bills amounting to Rs.25,542/-
(SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.2477/2021 which are marked at Ex.P.12 and the respondent No.2 has not elicited anything to disprove the same.

Therefore it is just and reasonable to award in all Rs.25,542/-
under the head medical expenses.

c) Towards food, extra nourishment, Conveyance and medical attendant charges: PW.1 has deposed that, immediately after accident he took treatment as an inpatient at Chandramma Dayanand Sagar from 15.03.2021 to 23.04.2021 i.e., for 40 days as per discharge summary marked at Ex.P.11.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 40 days and by including expenses of attendant of petitioner during the period of treatment and also by including conveyance, in all a sum of Rs.45,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant charges.

d) Towards Loss of Income during treatment:
 (SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.2477/2021
The petitioner contended that he was doing agriculture and milk vending work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
To proving the same, petitioner has not produced any document.

Therefore, in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to this Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
Accordingly, the fixed notional income of the year 2021 at 15,000/- p.m., Petitioner may took 3 months rest and he may lost income for those rest periods.
Therefore, by considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is entitled to Rs.45,000/- (Rs.15,000/- x 3) towards loss of income during treatment period.
e) Towards Future Earnings:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident he was inpatient in the hospital and has become permanently disabled.

The petitioner also examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara, as an (SCCH-9) 16 MVC.No.2477/2021 Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW.3 and he has contended that, on presentation he complaints of pain and difficulty in Ramesh Alias Ramesh V vs Nagesh Y on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175650736/

Regarding Liability:

The respondent No.2 has taken contention that, the owner of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-42-EB-9619 entrusted the said vehicle to the minor who did not had a valid and effective driving licence to ride the same on the date of the accident, which is the (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.2477/2021 vehicle involved in the accident violation of Section 3(1) of M.V.Act.

The jurisdictional police after due investigation have filed the charge sheet against the minor rider and owner of the motor cycle bearing reg.no.KA-42-EB-9619 and A1 and A2 under Section 181 of IMV Act by stating that, minor rider did not had a valid and effective driving licence to ride the same on the date of accident.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 has examined its Deputy Manager - Legal and from him got marked Ex.R.1 - copy of policy, Ex.R.2 - notice under Section 133, Ex.R.3 - reply to said notice.
During cross examination he has deposed that, rider of the offending motor cycle is minor and he did not had any driving licence.
So, it is purely violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Moreover, chargesheet has been registered in the name of rider of offending vehicle i.e., minor.
The petitioner has relied upon the citations relating to pay and recovery.
Among them one the citation which is (SCCH-9) 22 MVC.No.2477/2021 very apt to the present case in hand.

As per the decision reported in 2014 ACJ 2298 (Santosh Chhabra and others Vs. Abhishek Gureja and others)
wherein it is held that:
" Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Sections 149 (2) (A)(ii), 149 (4) and 149 (5) - Motor insurance - Minor - Driving licence - liability of Insurance company - Pay and recover order - Motor cycle driven by owner's minor son who had no driving licence hit a pedestrian and he sustained fatal injuries - Insurance company disputes its liability on the ground of breach of terms and conditions of policy - Tribunal directed owner of offending vehicle to pay compensation to the claimants exonerating insurance company from liability - Whether insurance company is duty - bound to take over contractual liability of the insured - Held:
yes; insurance company directed to pay compensation amount to the claimants at the first instance and thereafter recover the same from owner".

entities.text: 2014 ACJ 2298 (Santosh Chhabra and others Vs. Abhishek Gureja and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On perusal of the above said citation it came to know that, in said case also minor is entrusted by the owner of the motor cycle to rider the same without having any driving licence.
In the present case also the minor is the rider and here also RC owner i.e., father of minor rider has (SCCH-9) 23 MVC.No.2477/2021 entrusted his son to ride the same.

Therefore, it cannot be said that, Insurance Company is exonerated from the liability but in view of the above referred judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, the Insurance Company is liable to pay awarded compensation to recover from the respondent No.1.

Therefore, Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and recover the same from the respondent No.1 owner of the offending Motor cycle which involved in the accident is liable to pay the compensation amount of .6,89,542/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till realisation.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.3:
For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is partly (SCCH-9) 24 MVC.No.2477/2021 allowed with cost.

ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 15.03.2021 at about 9.00 am., near Shaneswaraswamy temple,
Ramanahalli-Mudavadi raod, Ramanahalli village, Ramanagara, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent act of riding of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-42-EB-9619 by its rider as alleged in the petition ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of rider of the offending motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-42-EB-9619 which belongs to the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is its insurer.
The petitioner contended that he was doing agriculture and milk vending work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 20% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
The respondent No.2 has taken contention that, the owner of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-42-EB-9619 entrusted the said vehicle to the minor who did not had a valid and effective driving licence to ride the same on the date of the accident, which is the (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.2477/2021 vehicle involved in the accident violation of Section 3(1) of M.V.Act.
The jurisdictional police after due investigation have filed the charge sheet against the minor rider and owner of the motor cycle bearing reg.no.KA-42-EB-9619 and A1 and A2 under Section 181 of IMV Act by stating that, minor rider did not had a valid and effective driving licence to ride the same on the date of accident.
So, it is purely violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Moreover, chargesheet has been registered in the name of rider of offending vehicle i.e., minor.
As per the decision reported in 2014 ACJ 2298 (Santosh Chhabra and others Vs. Abhishek Gureja and others)
wherein it is held that:
" Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Sections 149 (2) (A)(ii), 149 (4) and 149 (5) - Motor insurance - Minor - Driving licence - liability of Insurance company - Pay and recover order - Motor cycle driven by owner's minor son who had no driving licence hit a pedestrian and he sustained fatal injuries - Insurance company disputes its liability on the ground of breach of terms and conditions of policy - Tribunal directed owner of offending vehicle to pay compensation to the claimants exonerating insurance company from liability - Whether insurance company is duty - bound to take over contractual liability of the insured - Held:
yes; insurance company directed to pay compensation amount to the claimants at the first instance and thereafter recover the same from owner".
Therefore, it cannot be said that, Insurance Company is exonerated from the liability but in view of the above referred judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, the Insurance Company is liable to pay awarded compensation to recover from the respondent No.1.
Therefore, Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and recover the same from the respondent No.1 owner of the offending Motor cycle which involved in the accident is liable to pay the compensation amount of .6,89,542/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till realisation.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head future medical expenses which shall not carry any interest.
15. Issue No.3:
For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is partly (SCCH-9) 24 MVC.No.2477/2021 allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .6,89,542/- (Rupees six lakhs eighty nine thousand five hundred and forty two only) with interest at 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 - Insurer shall pay the compensation amount with interest at the first instance and recover the same from the respondent No.1 - R.C.Owner.
The respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 25% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 75% shall be released in favour of (SCCH-9) 25 MVC.No.2477/2021 petitioner on proper identification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
